component.name: ThermalPrint
component.summary: Design, prepare, and print thermal labels

description.p: ThermalPrint is a local workspace for designing, preparing, and printing labels on thermal label printers, with a native Linux desktop interface. It prints through CUPS, so it also works with regular laser and inkjet printers.

ul.li: Design labels with text, addresses, logos, shipping symbols, real barcodes (including GS1), and QR codes.
Import PDF and image labels from carriers and marketplaces, crop them, and print them in order.
Print numbered runs, merge a spreadsheet into a design, or place labels on an A4 or Letter sheet.
Print through CUPS, or export PDF, PNG, SVG, and ZPL.

description.p: Documents are processed on your computer; nothing is uploaded.

screenshot.caption: Importing and preparing a shipping label

description.p: Put your logo in the middle of a QR code.

ul.li: Add a logo to the center of any QR code in the Label Designer. It uses the highest error correction, the code is never smaller than version 5, and the logo size is limited so the code still scans.
A note tells you how wide to make the code so the logo scans, and a code that is too small for a logo is refused instead of printed unreadable.
The app opens on Home again. If labels were left in the queue, a Restore your last queue card on Home offers to bring them back.
A larger, more modern Home screen: big clickable cards, template tiles, recent documents as rows, and a printer chip.
A new row above the preview has previous and next buttons, a Reviewed checkbox, and a green Print button.
When Print is unavailable, pointing at it says why, such as "Tick Reviewed once you have checked the crop".

description.p: A smoother day of printing labels.

ul.li: The watch folder shows a Watching indicator, keeps trying if a drive disappears, and can print on its own printer.
Messages stay on screen long enough to read, with a history, and moving printed labels to Processed can be undone.
Thumbnails for the queue, Alt+Left and Alt+Right to move between labels, and Ctrl+Enter to print and go to the next.
The queue is remembered between sessions, Print all can skip a label that fails, and automatic crops can skip the review step.
A summary of what will print, a first-run checklist, and a check that every screen text is translated.
New option to move printed labels from the watch folder into a Processed folder, so the queue and the folder stay tidy.
Fixed new labels sometimes being missed by the watch folder when a file reused the name of an earlier one.
Saved .thermalprint files show a preview picture of the label in file managers (Debian and Fedora packages).
The Snap's helper now installs the file icon for your current icon theme, fixing a generic icon on themes such as Zorin.
ThermalPrint is made for thermal printers and also works with regular laser and inkjet printers.
The delete buttons in the address book, logo, and template lists now show a trash icon.
Symbol and logo previews are visible in dark mode.
Saved .thermalprint files now show the ThermalPrint icon in file managers.

description.p: More control in the Label Designer.

ul.li: Align, distribute, center, flip, lock, nudge with the arrow keys, smart guides, and a custom grid.
Text that wraps or shrinks to fit, line spacing, italic, inverse, and your own fonts.
Image dithering and contrast, barcode text options, and QR error correction.
See the printer's unprintable border and get a warning for objects inside it.
Print a numbered range, or several labels on an A4 or Letter sheet.
GS1-128 and GS1 Data Matrix barcodes with an SSCC helper.
QR codes from website, Wi-Fi, contact, email, and phone forms.
Shipping symbols, saved logos, an address book, and a template gallery with previews.
Auto-length labels for continuous rolls.
Unsaved changes are recovered after an unexpected exit.

description.p: Maintenance release: fixes building the user manual on older systems.
